body_en_plain:
Jan, 1997  No.113   Page Reply


 How to write to us...02     -

 Stephen Gregory......03    04

 Colin Bibby..........05    06

 Keith Taylor.........07    09

 Stephen Gregory......10    11

 George Munro.........14    18

   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

  Stephen Gregory, CHESTERFIELD

Dear Ron,

One of your subscribers (Dave
Knott in last month's OUTLET)was
enquiring about Mulftiface util-
ities...


GENIE:is a full disassembler and
was written by C. Lewis and D.
Gorski (not 3 so I suppose there
was not one for the +3)

LIFEGUARD:You could get on disk.

I own a Multiface 128 and had to
buy the above separately.

              Stephen Gregory

Brian Cavers to Stephen Gregory

Thanks, Stephen. I can add that
LIFEGUARD is a sort of PEEK and
POKE utility, often used to POKE
infinite lives, etc. in games.
It is provided with the Lunter
Spectrum emulator on the PC but
I think it is 'built-in' so you
can easily transfer it back to
the Spectrum I don't think. I
found it very useful when de-
bugging my disk modifications to
GRAPHIC ADVENTURE CREATOR (soon
to appear in OUTLET!).

There is also the possibility of
a utility in a future OUTLET to
give easier transfer of your own
code to the MF RAM.
                        Brian


From: Colin Bibby, MANCHESTER

Dear Ron,

Datel no longer stock the mouse,
etc. I have scoured the advert
columns but no luck.I would like
to assemble a suitable PCB for
myself and probably others. Are
you aware of any past projects
or PCBs for this job?

My friend Bill uses an Amiga/
Atari mouse (switchable) which
plugs in a DK'Tronics +3 inter-
face and works perfectly with
ARTIST II and IG. It operates as
a Kempston with both softwares.

                   Colin

Brian Cavers to Colin Bibby

Sorry your letter was just a
fraction too late to get into
last month's issue, Colin and I
also apologize that I had to
drastically reduce its size as I
don't get time these days to
type in lengthy letters. Text
files are much preferred! (disks
are returned) However, I believe
a lot of it was not really meant
for publication but just to let
us know who you are.

I have never heard of any mouse
DIY project but perhaps some of
our readers may write in with a
few tips in that regard. Mean-
while, I recommend you put an
advert in our OUTBOARD!
                        Brian

From: Keith Taylor




First of all let me wish you all
a merry Christmas and a great
new Year. Believe me I really
enjoy getting my regular copy
and hope to continue getting it
for a good while longer.


Now a word to Chris.. Thanks for
revising the program "LOT3" and
for mentioning my name.Now I can
claim my "15 minutes of fame".It
really made my day even though I
didn't recognise the finished
program!.



Just one point.When I originally
attempted to write the program,
it was just for fun.  However, I
am now running a syndicate and
use the same numbers each week
so could you please tell me how
to amend the program to:

(1). Add more selection lines
     and...

(2). Save the numbers entered.

Thanks.

                  Keith Taylor

Brian Cavers to Keith Taylor

I spent ten or fifteen minutes
looking at LOT3 and it was soon
clear that there is no quick fix
and it will need quite a bit of
re-writing. It might be possible
to get it to handle say, 20 or
possibly 40 in something like
its present form but with the
screen display much more comp-
acted but I wonder if that is
enough; some syndicates could be
hundreds. Perhaps the program
does not need to display all the
entries but could just display
them if 3 or more numbers are
drawn. Well, I'll pass this on
to Chris for his views and also
ask Ron if he might modify this
or his own lottery program.
                          Brian

From: Stephen Gregory


I have just received my first
OUTLET magazine and notice that
there is a reference No. on the
order form - do I have to quote
this when I get in touch?

Also, how do I advertise in the
magazine?

              Stephen Gregory

Ron Cavers to Stephen Gregory

No, you do not have to quote the
reference number on the order
form. A unique number is produc-
ed for each envelope we receive
for OUTLET magazine - whether it
be an order, letter, return or
contribution etc. This number is
then pencilled onto items rec-
eived - this ensures that disks,
diagrams, manuals, letters etc,
can easily be re-united and no-
thing gets lost. The number is
also printed onto the order form
so that we can quickly identify
what items, if any, need to be
returned.We use soft-lead pencil
or chinagraph pencil to mark the
number on items being returned -
this means nothing is defaced as
the number is easily erased.

This number also means that any
queries regarding orders etc are
quickly resolved.


For a small operation like ours,
this system sometimes looks a
bit over-the-top but when OUTLET
was first launched (in Sep '87)
Brian and I lived a hundred
miles apart so we had to set up
a system to cope with all sorts
of problems. This it does and,
even now - over eleven years
later, when Brian and I are now
just seven miles apart, the sys-
tem has proved its worth many
times over.



Re advertising:

Small adverts (no more than 10
screen lines) are published in
our OUTBOARD section. These can
be hand written, typed, or sent
in as a text file on a disk.
Larger ads can be included in
our OUTVERTS - but, in these
cases, we do ask that the ads
are sent on a disk. There is no
charge to readers for OUTBOARD
nor for the Spectrum version of
OUTVERTS. The PC OUTVERTS costs
`1 per 1K per month. You will
find more details on Page 1 of
each advertising section in OUT-
LET.

                          Ron

From:George B.Munro, LONDON, NW3

Dear Ron and Brian,

In addition to wishing a very
Merry Christmas and a Happy New
year to you all at OUTLET, I
thought that the following snip-
pet might be of interest and use
to fellow subscribers to the
OUTLET disc, particularly those
with +D Interfaces...

About two years ago I managed to
get hold of a partially u/s +D.
The fault was that it would only
operate one disc drive. This was
kept in reserve in case my main
+D gave up the ghost.  About two
months ago it did just that, so
I was left with only my standby
Interface.

Unfortunately that too ceased to
function and, with no-one doing
repairs on the +D, things were
to say the least of it DESPERATE
(notice here the difference in
spelling with SEPARATE)

Just why I took the following
action is beyond my comprehens-
ion, but, the +D was opened up,
each removable chip was taken
out, and in turn, very carefully
replaced, taking the greatest of
care to (a) put them back into
the same locations and facing
the same way as they previously
were and (b) to make sure that
all the little legs are properly
located in the appropriate slots
before pressing the chip fully
home. The latter is very import-


ant because you only get one try
at it and if the leg is bent by
mistake...I guess that would be
a real CATASTRASTROKE.

Once the top was replaced,making
sure that the LED comes into its
proper hole, the +Ds both worked
perfectly, and have continued to
do so to date.

Not being a technical wizard, I
can only assume that over the
years the contact between the
chip pins and their socket had
been somehow compromised, and
the action of removing and repl-
acing them had rectified this.It
leaves one wondering if a simi-
lar fault might occur in some of
our removable chips in our comp-


uters. Perhaps one of our tech-
nical subscribers might care to
comment.

Sorry to have been so longwinded
but I felt that there might be
some similarly poor distracted
soul out there, crying in their
beer, (or Coca-Cola) over the
demise of a well loved +D. I
would be interested to hear of
any recoveries achieved by this
method.

        Yours Aye,

        George B. Munro


Brian Cavers to George Munro

Thanks, George. I for one have
made a mental note of your comm-
ents and will certainly try it
if my +D just stops working for
no obvious reason. Mind you, it
occurred to me: could the prob-
lem have simply been a dirty
edge connector? Just removing a
+D interface and reconnecting it
is enough to give it a quick
clean (this is ALL I do these
days and it seems to be just as
effective as when I used to lab-
oriously clean the edge connect-
or with a rubber eraser! NOTE:
IMPORTANT! FOR ANYONE THAT DOES
NOT KNOW - NEVER REMOVE OR REPL-
ACE ANYTHING FROM OR TO A SPECT-
RUM UNLESS IT IS SWITCHED OFF AS
SERIOUS DAMAGE MAY BE DONE.Brian.

### How to write to us...

**PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!**

Text is accepted in any form for OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files (say which), typed or handwritten letters. However, PLEASE send us a textfile if possible so your letter needn't be typed again! The easiest for us to edit are Tasword 2 files with the right margin set at 32, but a textfile in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be parts of your letter you do not wish published, but we always use our discretion anyway. Letters may also be edited for clarity and length... Please ask if you welcome direct correspondence from other OUTLET readers and we will publish your full address.

---

### Stephen Gregory, CHESTERFIELD

Dear Ron,

One of your subscribers (Dave Knott in last month's OUTLET) was enquiring about Multiface utilities...

GENIE: is a full disassembler and was written by C. Lewis and D. Gorski (not 3 so I suppose there was not one for the +3)

LIFEGUARD: You could get on disk.

I own a Multiface 128 and had to buy the above separately.

— Stephen Gregory

**Brian Cavers to Stephen Gregory:**

Thanks, Stephen. I can add that LIFEGUARD is a sort of PEEK and POKE utility, often used to POKE infinite lives, etc. in games. It is provided with the Lunter Spectrum emulator on the PC, but I think it is 'built-in' so you can easily transfer it back to the Spectrum I don't think. I found it very useful when debugging my disk modifications to GRAPHIC ADVENTURE CREATOR (soon to appear in OUTLET!).

There is also the possibility of a utility in a future OUTLET to give easier transfer of your own code to the MF RAM.

— Brian

---

### From: Colin Bibby, MANCHESTER

Dear Ron,

Datel no longer stock the mouse, etc. I have scoured the advert columns but no luck. I would like to assemble a suitable PCB for myself and probably others. Are you aware of any past projects or PCBs for this job?

My friend Bill uses an Amiga/Atari mouse (switchable) which plugs in a DK'Tronics +3 interface and works perfectly with ARTIST II and IG. It operates as a Kempston with both softwares.

— Colin

**Brian Cavers to Colin Bibby:**

Sorry your letter was just a fraction too late to get into last month's issue, Colin, and I also apologize that I had to drastically reduce its size as I don't get time these days to type in lengthy letters. Text files are much preferred! (disks are returned) However, I believe a lot of it was not really meant for publication but just to let us know who you are.

I have never heard of any mouse DIY project but perhaps some of our readers may write in with a few tips in that regard. Meanwhile, I recommend you put an advert in our OUTBOARD!

— Brian

---

### From: Keith Taylor

First of all let me wish you all a merry Christmas and a great new Year. Believe me I really enjoy getting my regular copy and hope to continue getting it for a good while longer.

Now a word to Chris.. Thanks for revising the program "LOT3" and for mentioning my name. Now I can claim my "15 minutes of fame". It really made my day even though I didn't recognise the finished program!.

Just one point. When I originally attempted to write the program, it was just for fun. However, I am now running a syndicate and use the same numbers each week so could you please tell me how to amend the program to:

(1). Add more selection lines and...

(2). Save the numbers entered.

Thanks.

— Keith Taylor

**Brian Cavers to Keith Taylor:**

I spent ten or fifteen minutes looking at LOT3 and it was soon clear that there is no quick fix and it will need quite a bit of re-writing. It might be possible to get it to handle say, 20 or possibly 40 in something like its present form but with the screen display much more compacted, but I wonder if that is enough; some syndicates could be hundreds. Perhaps the program does not need to display all the entries but could just display them if 3 or more numbers are drawn. Well, I'll pass this on to Chris for his views and also ask Ron if he might modify this or his own lottery program.

— Brian

---

### From: Stephen Gregory

I have just received my first OUTLET magazine and notice that there is a reference No. on the order form — do I have to quote this when I get in touch?

Also, how do I advertise in the magazine?

— Stephen Gregory

**Ron Cavers to Stephen Gregory:**

No, you do not have to quote the reference number on the order form. A unique number is produced for each envelope we receive for OUTLET magazine — whether it be an order, letter, return or contribution etc. This number is then pencilled onto items received — this ensures that disks, diagrams, manuals, letters etc, can easily be re-united and nothing gets lost. The number is also printed onto the order form so that we can quickly identify what items, if any, need to be returned. We use soft-lead pencil or chinagraph pencil to mark the number on items being returned — this means nothing is defaced as the number is easily erased.

This number also means that any queries regarding orders etc are quickly resolved.

For a small operation like ours, this system sometimes looks a bit over-the-top, but when OUTLET was first launched (in Sep '87) Brian and I lived a hundred miles apart so we had to set up a system to cope with all sorts of problems. This it does and, even now — over eleven years later, when Brian and I are now just seven miles apart, the system has proved its worth many times over.

Re advertising:

Small adverts (no more than 10 screen lines) are published in our OUTBOARD section. These can be handwritten, typed, or sent in as a text file on a disk. Larger ads can be included in our OUTVERTS — but, in these cases, we do ask that the ads are sent on a disk. There is no charge to readers for OUTBOARD nor for the Spectrum version of OUTVERTS. The PC OUTVERTS costs £1 per 1K per month. You will find more details on Page 1 of each advertising section in OUTLET.

— Ron

---

### From: George B. Munro, LONDON, NW3

Dear Ron and Brian,

In addition to wishing a very Merry Christmas and a Happy New year to you all at OUTLET, I thought that the following snippet might be of interest and use to fellow subscribers to the OUTLET disc, particularly those with +D Interfaces...

About two years ago I managed to get hold of a partially u/s +D. The fault was that it would only operate one disc drive. This was kept in reserve in case my main +D gave up the ghost. About two months ago it did just that, so I was left with only my standby Interface.

Unfortunately that too ceased to function and, with no-one doing repairs on the +D, things were to say the least of it DESPERATE (notice here the difference in spelling with SEPARATE).

Just why I took the following action is beyond my comprehension, but the +D was opened up, each removable chip was taken out, and in turn, very carefully replaced, taking the greatest of care to (a) put them back into the same locations and facing the same way as they previously were and (b) to make sure that all the little legs are properly located in the appropriate slots before pressing the chip fully home. The latter is very important because you only get one try at it and if the leg is bent by mistake... I guess that would be a real CATASTRASTROKE.

Once the top was replaced, making sure that the LED comes into its proper hole, the +Ds both worked perfectly, and have continued to do so to date.

Not being a technical wizard, I can only assume that over the years the contact between the chip pins and their socket had been somehow compromised, and the action of removing and replacing them had rectified this. It leaves one wondering if a similar fault might occur in some of our removable chips in our computers. Perhaps one of our technical subscribers might care to comment.

Sorry to have been so longwinded but I felt that there might be some similarly poor distracted soul out there, crying in their beer (or Coca-Cola) over the demise of a well loved +D. I would be interested to hear of any recoveries achieved by this method.

Yours Aye,

George B. Munro

**Brian Cavers to George Munro:**

Thanks, George. I for one have made a mental note of your comments and will certainly try it if my +D just stops working for no obvious reason. Mind you, it occurred to me: could the problem have simply been a dirty edge connector? Just removing a +D interface and reconnecting it is enough to give it a quick clean (this is ALL I do these days and it seems to be just as effective as when I used to laboriously clean the edge connector with a rubber eraser! NOTE: IMPORTANT! FOR ANYONE THAT DOES NOT KNOW — NEVER REMOVE OR REPLACE ANYTHING FROM OR TO A SPECTRUM UNLESS IT IS SWITCHED OFF AS SERIOUS DAMAGE MAY BE DONE.

— Brian

### Как написать нам...

**ПОЖАЛУЙСТА, ПРИСЫЛАЙТЕ ТЕКСТОВЫЕ ФАЙЛЫ!**

Для рубрики OUTLETTERS тексты принимаются в любом виде: файлы текстовых процессоров (уточняйте, каких именно), напечатанные на машинке или рукописные письма. Однако, ПОЖАЛУЙСТА, по возможности присылайте нам текстовый файл, чтобы ваше письмо не приходилось набирать заново! Проще всего нам редактировать файлы Tasword 2 с правым полем, установленным на 32 символа, но мы будем рады текстовому файлу в ЛЮБОМ формате!

Пожалуйста, укажите, если какие-то фрагменты письма вы не хотите публиковать, хотя мы в любом случае действуем по своему усмотрению. Письма также могут быть отредактированы для ясности и сокращения объема... Пожалуйста, сообщите, если вы не против прямой переписки с другими читателями OUTLET, и мы опубликуем ваш полный адрес.

---

### Stephen Gregory, CHESTERFIELD

Дорогой Ron,

Один из ваших подписчиков (Dave Knott в прошлом номере OUTLET) интересовался утилитами для Multiface...

GENIE: это полноценный дизассемблер, написанный C. Lewis и D. Gorski (не для +3, так что, полагаю, версии под +3 не существовало).

LIFEGUARD: можно было купить на диске.

Я владею Multiface 128, и мне пришлось докупать эти программы отдельно.

— Stephen Gregory

**Brian Cavers отвечает Stephen Gregory:**

Спасибо, Stephen. Добавлю, что LIFEGUARD — это своего рода утилита PEEK и POKE, которую часто используют для бесконечных жизней и других читов в играх. Она входит в состав эмулятора Spectrum от Lunter на PC, но, по-моему, она там «встроена», так что вряд ли ее удастся легко перенести обратно на реальный Spectrum. Мне она очень пригодилась при отладке дисковых модификаций для GRAPHIC ADVENTURE CREATOR (скоро появится в OUTLET!).

Также есть вероятность, что в одном из будущих номеров OUTLET выйдет утилита для более удобной передачи собственного кода в ОЗУ Multiface.

— Brian

---

### От: Colin Bibby, MANCHESTER

Дорогой Ron,

В Datel закончились мыши и сопутствующие товары. Я прочесал все разделы объявлений, но безрезультатно. Я хотел бы сам спаять подходящую плату для себя и, возможно, для других. Известны ли вам какие-либо прежние радиолюбительские схемы или печатные платы для этой задачи?

Мой друг Bill использует переключаемую мышь Amiga/Atari, которая подключается к интерфейсу DK'Tronics +3 и отлично работает с ARTIST II и IG. В обеих программах она функционирует как Kempston-мышь.

— Colin

**Brian Cavers отвечает Colin Bibby:**

Жаль, Colin, твое письмо опоздало буквально на чуть-чуть, чтобы попасть в прошлый номер. Также прошу прощения за то, что пришлось сильно сократить его объем: сейчас у меня совсем нет времени перенабирать длинные рукописи. Текстовые файлы куда предпочтительнее! (дискеты мы возвращаем). Впрочем, мне показалось, что большая часть текста и не предназначалась для печати, а скорее служила знакомством.

О самодельных схемах подключения мыши я ничего не слышал, но, возможно, кто-то из наших читателей напишет пару советов на этот счет. А пока советую дать объявление в нашей рубрике OUTBOARD!

— Brian

---

### От: Keith Taylor

Прежде всего, поздравляю всех с прошедшим Рождеством и наступившим Новым годом. Поверьте, я с огромным удовольствием получаю каждый свежий выпуск и надеюсь выписывать журнал еще очень долго.

Пара слов для Chris: спасибо за доработку программы «LOT3» и за то, что упомянул мое имя! Теперь я могу заявить о своих «15 минутах славы». Это по-настоящему подняло мне настроение, хотя в готовом виде я свою программу даже не узнал!.

Только один момент. Когда я изначально пробовал написать эту программу, это было просто ради забавы. Однако теперь я организовал лотерейный синдикат, и каждую неделю мы используем одни и те же номера. Не могли бы вы подсказать, как изменить программу, чтобы:

(1). Добавить больше строк выбора билетов и...

(2). Сохранять введенные числа.

Спасибо.

— Keith Taylor

**Brian Cavers отвечает Keith Taylor:**

Я уделил LOT3 минут десять-пятнадцать, и быстро стало ясно, что простым исправлением тут не обойтись — потребуется изрядная переработка. Возможно, удастся заставить ее обрабатывать, скажем, 20 или 40 вариантов в близком к нынешнему виде, если сильно уплотнить экран, но хватит ли этого? В некоторых синдикатах число участников доходит до сотен. Быть может, программе и не нужно выводить все билеты на экран, а показывать только те, где совпало 3 и более номеров. В общем, я передам вопрос Chris, чтобы узнать его мнение, а также спрошу Ron — вдруг он захочет доработать эту или свою собственную лотерейную программу.

— Brian

---

### От: Stephen Gregory

Я только что получил свой первый выпуск журнала OUTLET и заметил номер заказа на бланке — нужно ли мне указывать его при обращении к вам?

И еще: как подать объявление в журнал?

— Stephen Gregory

**Ron Cavers отвечает Stephen Gregory:**

Нет, указывать номер с бланка заказа не обязательно. Уникальный номер присваивается каждому конверту, поступающему в редакцию OUTLET — будь то заказ, письмо, возврат дискеты или авторский материал. Этот номер затем аккуратно проставляется карандашом на всех вложенных предметах: так диски, схемы, инструкции, письма гарантированно не перепутаются и не потеряются. Этот же номер печатается на бланке заказа, чтобы мы могли мгновенно понять, что именно (если требуется) нужно вернуть отправителю. Для пометок на возвращаемых вещах мы используем мягкий простой карандаш или стеклографический карандаш (chinagraph) — он легко стирается и ничего не портит.

Кроме того, благодаря этому номеру любые вопросы по заказам решаются за считанные минуты.

Для такого скромного предприятия, как наше, подобная система может показаться чересчур бюрократичной, но когда OUTLET только зарождался (в сентябре 1987 года), мы с Brian жили в ста милях друг от друга, поэтому нам требовался надежный механизм на все случаи жизни. Он отлично работает, и даже сейчас — спустя более чем одиннадцать лет, когда нас разделяет всего семь миль — система доказала свою полезность бесчисленное множество раз.

Что касается рекламы:

Небольшие объявления (не более 10 экранных строк) публикуются в нашей рубрике OUTBOARD. Их можно присылать рукописными, напечатанными на машинке или в виде текстового файла на диске.
